land.text: Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained Lothair I's after Verdun, with Aachen

predecessors.note: Lothair I died on 19 September 855 at Prüm; the Treaty of Prüm gave Lothair II 'Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained his father's after the Treaty of Verdun'. Louis II took Italy and Charles Provence and the greater part of Burgundy (lower-burgundy).

land.text: eastern Austrasia with Aachen and Metz, most of Frisia and most of Upper Burgundy

successors.note: Treaty of Meerssen, 8 August 870: Louis the German took the eastern part with Aachen and Metz and most of Frisia. Hugh, Lothair's illegitimate son, 'was granted the Duchy of Alsace'.

union.text: western Lotharingia: Cliopatria's 870 addition (Meuse west bank, Brabant, Hainaut, Flanders side)

land.text: west of the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône line, with Lyon, Vienne and Besançon

successors.note: Treaty of Meerssen: Charles the Bald took Lothair's Lower Burgundy inheritance (Lyon and Vienne) and a small western part of Upper Burgundy with Besançon; the border ran roughly along the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône.

capitals.name: Aachen
capitals.note: 'ruled from Aachen and did not venture outside his kingdom' (Lotharingia page); 'the capital of Aachen' (Treaty of Prüm page). Lothair II hosted the Council of Metz in 863.

rulers.name: Lothair II
rulers.note: Acceded September 855; died 7 August 869 at Piacenza, with no legitimate children. His heir was his brother Louis II of Italy, away at Bari; his uncles Louis the German and Charles the Bald took the inheritance (Meerssen page). No king 869-870.

correction.text: Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained Lothair I's after Verdun, with Aachen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Lotharingia for 855-859 and draws Lothair II's realm as Lower Burgundy 860-869). The Treaty of Prüm page: 'Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained his father's after the Treaty of Verdun'; the Lotharingia page adds present-day Lorraine, Luxembourg, parts of Switzerland and Germany west of the Rhine, most of Belgium and the Netherlands. The gazetteer region Lotharingia is the reading; neither page gives a frontier. No infobox area on either page.

union.text: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble

correction.text: Lothair II's kingdom with the Lyonnais and the Viennois received in 863

keyframe_review.note: 863-870: the Lyonnais and the Viennois added on Charles of Provence's death (24 January 863). This is the territory Cliopatria draws as Lower Burgundy 866-869 (157,801 km2; the lower-burgundy dossier handles that row). Held without a king from 7 August 869 until the Treaty of Meerssen (8 August 870).

region.text: Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained Lothair I's after Verdun, with Aachen

ledger.note: 855: Lothair I dies and Lothair II inherits the north of Middle Francia. 'Lothair II was granted Frisia and the parts of Austrasia that remained his father's after the Treaty of Verdun' (Treaty of Prüm page, 19 September 855); the Lotharingia page: 'In 855, when Lothair I was dying in Prüm Abbey, he divided his kingdom among his three sons'; the Lothair II page: 'was given Lothair I's territory between Frisia and the Alps'. The pages give lands, not a boundary.

region.text: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble

ledger.note: 863: Charles of Provence dies on 24 January and Lothair II takes the Lyonnais and the Viennois, Louis II taking the rest of Provence. 'received the Lyonnais and the Viennois' (Lothair II page). The region is the lower-burgundy dossier's, which adds Grenoble from another page; this page names only Lyon and Vienne.

union.text: western Lotharingia: Cliopatria's 870 addition (Meuse west bank, Brabant, Hainaut, Flanders side)

region.text: west of the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône line, with Lyon, Vienne and Besançon

ledger.note: 870: The Treaty of Meerssen gives Charles the Bald the west of Lothair's realm. 'Charles received Lothair's inheritance in Lower Burgundy (including Lyon and Vienne)' and 'a small western part of Upper Burgundy' with Besançon; 'The borderline ran roughly along the rivers Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saone and Rhone.' The region is the west-franks dossier's mirror of this loss (it adds the western Lotharingian cells from the Cliopatria 870 West Franks shape, which the Meerssen page does not itemise).

region.text: eastern Austrasia with Aachen and Metz, most of Frisia and most of Upper Burgundy

ledger.note: 870: The Treaty of Meerssen gives Louis the German the east. Louis took 'his eastern part including both Aachen and Metz, and most of Frisia'; he joined central Austrasia to Louis the Younger's subkingdom; Hugh 'was granted the Duchy of Alsace'. The region is the east-franks dossier's mirror (Cliopatria's 870 East Franks addition).

union.text: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble

region.text: the whole kingdom, divided at Meerssen between Louis the German and Charles the Bald

ledger.note: 870: Lothair II's kingdom ends, a year after his death. 'In 869, Lothair II died without legitimate children'; 'his uncles, Louis the German and Charles the Bald, took his inheritance'; 'Charles had himself crowned in Metz the same year', but his brother forced him to partition Lotharingia 'as they had agreed at Metz in 868'. Treaty of Meerssen, 8 August 870. East Francia held its share to 880 (Ribemont), when Louis the Younger took western Lotharingia (Lotharingia page).

wars.name: Succession to Lothair II (Treaty of Meerssen)

union.text: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble

zones.text: Lothair II's whole realm, claimed by Charles the Bald and Louis the German; the heir Louis II of Italy was fighting the Emirate of Bari

wars.outcome: Charles crowned himself at Metz in 869; his brother forced a partition, agreed at Metz in 868 and made at Meerssen on 8 August 870 along roughly the Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saône and Rhône.
wars.note: The east-franks and west-franks dossiers carry the 869-870 contest over the whole realm.

certainty.note: The partition of 855 names lands (Frisia, Austrasia, Aachen), not a frontier, and the Meerssen line of 870 runs 'roughly' along rivers; the realm 'lacked ethnic or linguistic unity' and its frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes: Written for eu-07-x from four pages (Lothair II, Lotharingia, Treaty of Meerssen, Treaty of Prüm). This is Lothair II's kingdom 855-870; Zwentibold's kingdom 895-900 is kingdom-of-lotharingia-zwentibold (eu-07-d) and the duchy from 903 has no dossier yet. Cliopatria has no Lotharingia for 855-859 and draws the realm as Lower Burgundy 860-869 (860-865: 209,031 km2, which also contains Charles of Provence's Provence; 866-869: 157,801 km2); the lower-burgundy dossier (eu-07-e) writes that row against Charles's kingdom, so the two dossiers must not both draw the 860-865 northern part. The gazetteer region 'Lotharingia' (703 cells, about 178,000 km2) is the 855 reading. The 863 region is the lower-burgundy dossier's (Lyon, Vienne, Grenoble); the 870 regions are the west-franks and east-franks dossiers' mirror specs (their Cliopatria-difference form), so the cells match; this page itself names Lyon, Vienne, Aachen, Metz, Frisia, Besançon and a rough river line only. State kept alive to 8 August 870 (Meerssen) so the sibling dossiers' 870 gains from kingdom-of-lotharingia have a counterpart; east-franks and west-franks record the 869-870 contest over the whole realm. Not on the pages (not drawn): 856 Treaty of Orbe (Lothair II page mentions it; the Prüm page is silent); 859 grant of Hucbert's territories to Louis II (region not given; a gap-filler should open 'Hucbert' and 'Transjurane Burgundy'); 867 Alsace to Hugh (internal); the 868 Metz agreement; the extent of Upper Burgundy in Lothair's hands 855-870. The east-franks dossier says 'most of Upper Burgundy' went east; the Meerssen page gives Charles only 'a small western part'. No infobox area on any page, so no area comparison. Lothair II died 7 August 869 (Lothair II page), not 8 August as some lists give.
